title: Γυνὴ καὶ ὄρνις
part: The Widow and the Hen (Chambry 90 · Perry 58)
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 90 (= Perry 58). Text as printed. Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Γυνή τις χήρα ὄρνιν εἶχε καθ’ ἑκάστην ἡμέραν ᾠὸν αὐτῇ τίκτουσαν.
sentences.tr: Gynē tis chēra ornin eiche kath’ hekastēn hēmeran ōion autēi tiktousan.
sentences.l: A certain widow had a hen laying her an egg every day.
sentences.n: ὄρνις covers both 'bird' and 'hen'; the egg settles it here, and the fable is read as a hen throughout. αὐτῇ is a dative of advantage, 'laid an egg for her'.

sentences.t: Νομίσασα δὲ ὥς, εἰ πλείους τῇ ὄρνιθι κριθὰς παραβάλλοι, δὶς τέξεται τῆς ἡμέρας, τοῦτο πεποίηκεν.
sentences.tr: Nomisasa de hōs, ei pleious tēi ornithi krithas paraballoi, dis texetai tēs hēmeras, touto pepoiēken.
sentences.l: And having supposed that, if she should throw more barley to the hen, it would lay twice in the day, she has done this.
sentences.n: ὡς introduces indirect statement after νομίσασα, with the optative παραβάλλοι in the protasis — her reasoning held at arm's length — and the future τέξεται in the apodosis. τῆς ἡμέρας is a genitive of time within which. πεποίηκεν is a perfect where a narrative aorist would be expected; Chambry prints it so.

sentences.t: Ἡ δ’ ὄρνις πιμελὴς γενομένη οὐδ’ ἅπαξ τῆς ἡμέρας τεκεῖν ἠδύνατο.
sentences.tr: Hē d’ ornis pimelēs genomenē oud’ hapax tēs hēmeras tekein ēdynato.
sentences.l: But the hen, having grown fat, was not able to lay even once in the day.

sentences.t: Ὁ μῦθος δηλοῖ ὅτι οἱ διὰ πλεονεξίαν τῶν πλειόνων ἐπιθυμοῦντες καὶ τὰ παρόντα ἀποβάλλουσι.
sentences.tr: Ho mythos dēloi hoti hoi dia pleonexian tōn pleionōn epithymountes kai ta paronta apoballousi.
sentences.l: The fable shows that those who out of greed desire more throw away what they have as well.
sentences.n: τὰ παρόντα, 'the things at hand', is the standing phrase for what one already possesses. The καί is 'as well': the loss comes on top of the gain never made.
